newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crudes edge down, Minas premium up to 15 cts.
newsitem.headline: Asia crudes edge down, Minas premium up to 15 cts.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were slightly lower on Friday as futures prices continued to pare gains from the recent rally.
SIMEX November Brent futures fell three cents to $21.88 per barrel and London slipped a further four cents to stand at $21.84 in late afternoon Asia time.
NYMEX October crude, which fell 35 cents in New York to $23.54 was last traded on the overnight ACCESS system at $23.38.
The weaker tone to the futures market narrowed the Brent/Dubai spread for November to $2.05/$2.12 in late trading, compared with a day-earlier spread of $2.12/$2.22.
A December Brent/Dubai was traded between a U.S. refiner and a trader at $2.04 late on Thursday.
Dubai intermonth spreads remained mostly steady on recent day's trading at around 40 cents for November/December and December/January.

Players have locked in the 40 cent Dubai spread this week. A Jan/Feb Dubai spread was done at 40 cents late Thursday between a major and a trader, while a trader and a state oil group exchanged a December/February spread at 82 cents.
October paper Tapis rose to $22.05/$22.25 late Friday from $21.90/$22.30 earlier but was down on Thursday's $22.15/$22.40.
In wet trading a producer sold 200,000 barrels of Minas to Japan at ICP quotes plus 15 cents -- the highest premium so far for October barrels.
Traders said equity holders had little Minas left for October. One said it had a top-up cargo available only and would be asking plus 20 cents.
A third November Murban cargo traded at ADNOC plus 19.5 cents between two majors, matching the previous deal and topping the first by 0.5 cent, traders said.
